newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds open slightly stronger but quiet.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds open slightly stronger but quiet.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened slightly firmer in light trading on Friday and were expected to remain quiet ahead of the weekend, analysts said.

"Going into the weekend, the tone in the treasury market is not positive," said Andrew Pyle, head of fixed-income research at ABN-AMRO Bank Canada. The Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia said on Thursday that its business activity index soared in June, prompting fears that the U.S. economy was overheating.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.21 to C$116.72 to yield 6.698 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 2/32 to yield 6.68 percent. The negative spread between the two bonds narrowed to two basis points from three at Thursday's close.
"There's no news out there," said Michael Gregory, Lehman Brothers fixed-income economist.

Market players will keep an eye on this weekend's G7 summit. The seven member nations and Russia could discuss foreign currency exchange, Gregory said. In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.20 to C$106.85 to yield 6.036 percent, while the U.S. 10-year rose 4/32 to yield 6.38 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 34 basis points from 26 basis points at Thursday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.79 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.08 percent.
